Questions.Question: How many players can a club put on its main squad list?
How many places in the main squad list are reserved for locally trained players, and how many of those can be association-trained?
Questions.Answer: According to paragraph [31.04], a minimum of eight places on List A are reserved exclusively for locally trained players. Out of these eight places, no more than four can be association-trained players.

Questions.Question: A club registers a new player during the qualifying phase and that takes List A to 26 names. What must it do?
Questions.Answer: If the registration of a new player during the qualifying phase causes the number of players on List A to exceed 25, the club must remove the necessary number of currently registered players to reduce List A to 25 players again, in compliance with the quota of locally trained players.

Questions.Question: What is the minimum number of goalkeepers a club must register?
What are the age and tenure conditions for putting a young player on List B?
Questions.Answer:
According to regulation [31.12], a young player can be registered on List B if they meet the following conditions:

1. They are born on or after 1 January 2004.
2. They have been eligible to play for the club concerned for an uninterrupted period of two years since their 15th birthday, or a total of three consecutive years with a maximum of one loan period to a club from the same association for up to one year.
3. Players aged 16 may be registered on List B if they have been registered with the participating club for the previous two years without interruption.

Questions.Question: Can a club add new players to its squad after the league phase ends?
Questions.Answer: Yes, a club may register new players after the league phase ends and before the start of the knockout phase. As per Paragraph 32.01, a club may register a maximum of three new eligible players by 5 February 2026 (24:00 CET) for the remaining matches in the competition. Additionally, if certain exceptional conditions outlined in Paragraph 32.02 are met (e.g., more than five or seven players on List A are no longer registered with the national association), clubs participating in domestic championships that follow the calendar year format may be entitled to register up to four or five new eligible players, respectively.

Questions.Question: How many substitutions is a team allowed during a match?
What happens if a knockout tie is level after both legs?
What share of stadium capacity has to be made available to visiting supporters, and is there a price limit?
Questions.Answer: At least 5% of the stadium's UEFA spectator capacity must be made available to visiting supporters. The price of tickets for visiting supporters must not exceed the price paid by home supporters for comparable sectors and in no case shall exceed €50.

Questions.Question: How many medals do the winning and losing finalists receive?
Questions.Answer: The winning team is presented with 50 gold medals, and the runner-up is presented with 50 silver medals.

Questions.Question: If a club only has six locally trained players available, what happens to the size of its squad?
Two clubs finish the league phase on the same number of points. How is the higher position decided?
Questions.Answer: If two clubs finish the league phase on the same number of points, their ranking is determined by the following tiebreaking criteria in order: (1) superior goal difference in the league phase, (2) higher number of goals scored in the league phase, (3) higher number of away goals scored in the league phase, (4) higher number of wins in the league phase, (5) higher number of away wins in the league phase, (6) higher number of points obtained collectively by league phase opponents, (7) superior collective goal difference of league phase opponents, (8) higher number of goals scored collectively by league phase opponents, (9) lower disciplinary points total based on yellow and red cards received, (10) higher club coefficient. (Regulation 18.01)

Questions.Question: A player is sent off in the last league phase match. Does that suspension carry into the knockout rounds?
Questions.Answer: Yes, a player sent off in the last league phase match is automatically suspended for the next match in the UEFA club competition, which includes the knockout rounds. According to Paragraph 63.01, a player sent off is automatically suspended for the next match in the competition, and there are no exceptions outlined in the regulations that would nullify this suspension when entering the knockout phase.

Questions.Question: A club's first-choice goalkeeper is injured for two months. Can they bring in a replacement, and does the replacement have to be locally trained?
How long must an outfield player be out before he can be replaced, and is that the same threshold as for a goalkeeper?
Two clubs turn up with clashing shirts. Who has to change — and is the answer different in the final?
Questions.Answer: During the final, if there is a colour clash, the team designated as the away team must wear alternative colours (40.03). For non-final matches, if the referee notices on the spot that the colours of the two teams could lead to confusion, the home team must change colours as a rule (40.02).

Questions.Question: Can two clubs owned by the same investment group both play in this competition?
Questions.Answer: No, two clubs owned by the same investment group cannot both participate in the UEFA Champions League. As per Paragraph 5.01, no club participating in a UEFA club competition may directly or indirectly hold or deal in the securities or shares of another participating club, or be involved in its management, administration, or sporting performance. Furthermore, under Paragraph 5.01(cc), no individual or legal entity may have control or influence over more than one participating club, where 'control or influence' includes holding a majority of voting rights, appointing key members, or exercising decisive influence over the club.

Questions.Question: A match is abandoned at half-time and resumed the following day. Which players can take the field?
Does a player's passport determine whether he counts toward the domestic development requirement?
Questions.Answer: No, a player's passport does not determine whether he counts toward the domestic development requirement. A player's status as a club-trained or association-trained player depends on the duration and timing of the player's registration with the club (31.06) or with other clubs affiliated with the same national association (31.07), rather than their nationality or passport.

Questions.Question: A player left off both squad lists picks up a ban. Can he sit it out while unregistered?
Questions.Answer: No, only players who are duly registered with UEFA on List A or List B can validly serve pending suspensions.

Questions.Question: After a defeat, is the head coach personally required to speak to broadcasters, and how quickly must the press conference start?
Questions.Answer: Yes, the head coach is personally required to speak to broadcasters after a defeat, as the regulations specify that the head coach must be available for interviews with audiovisual rights-holders (paragraph 80.01). Additionally, the post-match press conference must start no later than 20 minutes after the final whistle (paragraph 80.02).

Questions.Question: Can a club choose which ball is used for its home fixtures?
Questions.Answer: No, a club cannot freely choose which ball is used for its home fixtures. For matches in the qualifying phase, the balls must comply with the IFAB Laws of the Game and UEFA Equipment Regulations, as specified in paragraph 50.01. From the play-offs onwards, the official UEFA Champions League match ball determined by the UEFA administration must be used, as stated in paragraph 50.02.

Questions.Question: Does Liverpool's registered squad satisfy the locally trained player requirement?
Questions.Answer: No, Liverpool's registered squad does not satisfy the locally trained player requirement. According to paragraph [31.04], at least 8 places on List A must be reserved for locally trained players (club-trained and association-trained). Liverpool's squad consists of 20 players in total, among which only 5 are locally trained (3 club-trained and 2 association-trained).

Questions.Question: Manchester United are short on club-trained players. How many can they actually register on List A as things stand?
Questions.Answer: Manchester United currently have 3 club-trained players. According to paragraph [31.04], if a club has fewer than eight locally trained players (club-trained plus association-trained) on List A, the maximum number of players that can be registered is reduced accordingly. Since Manchester United have only 3 club-trained players and 5 association-trained players, they meet the requirement of 8 locally trained players, allowing them to register the full 25 players on List A.

Questions.Question: Real Madrid have registered the goalkeepers shown in their squad. Are they compliant on that front?
Questions.Answer: Yes, Real Madrid are compliant. They have registered two goalkeepers, Thibaut Courtois and Andriy Lunin, on List A. Per regulation [31.13], a club must have at least two goalkeepers on List A and at least three in total (List A and List B combined). To confirm total compliance, inclusion of a third goalkeeper on List B should be ensured, as List B details are not provided here.
